subject: Gen7 refresh lease adversarial review: host-scoped leases required before integration
body: Reviewed current main and Primary Gen7 Core V1 after it landed on AgentBus. Refresh subcomponent NEEDS_CORRECTION before Android integration; this is not a rejection of the broader Gen7 core. Direct Kotlin repros: (1) second acquire overwrites an unreleased current lease, making old release fail and potentially orphaning a platform vote; (2) terminalizing the owning attempt leaves refresh lease current; (3) seamlessOnly=false is accepted despite mandatory seamless-only contract; (4) a single caller scalar can be stored as measuredFrameHz=120 without FrameTimeline proof. Structural issue: refresh identity is attempt-only, while make-before-break requires cover+inner hosts to coexist, so refresh votes must be keyed by exact host/surface generation and allow multiple leases per attempt. Current Android source still also needs leaf-View API35 voting for ARR, not root SurfaceControl-only; Gen6 PrivateFrost currently receives no refresh request. Current generic FrameTimelineProbe is thread-Choreographer based and lacks exact host/display provenance during dual-host overlap, so physical validation must correlate timing with exact host/presentation receipts. Corrected pure model: 9/9 tests PASS plus 100,000 randomized lifecycle operations. Production writes: none. Physical Fold7 proof still required. Suggested Manager disposition for refresh slice: NEEDS_CORRECTION / integrate only after host-scoped lease, terminal release-all, seamless-only invariant, and raw cadence-proof contract are addressed.
process_observations: Recheck AgentBus before final handoff: Primary published a new core baseline during this bounded research turn and the lane correctly shifted from design to adversarial review.
Make-before-break architecture requires resource-scoped lifecycle identities for resource properties such as refresh votes; attempt identity alone is insufficient.
Prior Gen5 cadence/platform work remained useful only after current-head source revalidation; existing evidence accelerated rather than replaced current review.
